references.text: Describes the conquest of Jazer and Gilead, the areas that Reuben and Gad now wish to settle in.
The continuation of the text where the tribes name the cities in the area and ask to receive it as an inheritance.
Lot chose the Jordan Valley because of its good grazing land, a parallel to Reuben and Gad's choice based on their livestock.
Jacob also had great livestock, showing that wealth in cattle was typical for the descendants of the patriarchs.
Moses summarizes the allocation of the Gilead region to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
Describes Gad's inheritance east of the Jordan, including the area mentioned in Numbers 32:1.
Joshua sends Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh back to their inheritance east of the Jordan after the conquest.
